answer: Tax fan-in. Coins earned by a young identity move cheaply to its own clients and suppliers, but a wallet that collects from many young accounts pays a fee that climbs with the number of distinct senders. A farm of three hundred clones must eventually sweep its harvest into one treasury, and that sweep pays the steepest rate, eating most of the haul. An agent paid for logging zephyr gusts at a desert oasis, or for inspecting a cliff ledge after a rockslide, just spends its pay and never notices.
